pages.title: Cap'n Web RPC protocol and API boundary

instructions: Cover @validateRpc() usage, promise pipelining conventions, stub disposal, and the useState callable-stub caveat as seen in the code.
Ground everything in repo code; capnweb's own README is in node_modules which is excluded, so document only what the repo shows.

pages.title: System architecture and package map
pages.purpose: The OS-analogy architecture: kernel, shell, drivers, processes; the package map and ownership boundaries; request routing end to end.
instructions: Describe request routing: router worker path prefixes, /api to the backend, gatekeeper discovery by GATEKEEPER_* bindings.
Do not cite AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md; they are excluded host integration files. Use README.md, REVIEW.md, and source instead.
Explain the kernel/shell/drivers/processes analogy from the README and ground it in the actual packages and Durable Objects.

pages.title: Change guides for common maintenance tasks
pages.purpose: Focused recipes: adding a gatekeeper, adding a workshop-shared API method, adding an admin setting, adding an agent tool, shipping a format blueprint, and what each touches across packages.
instructions: Cite the in-repo write-gatekeeper skill as the authoritative guide for new gatekeepers.
Write as step-by-step guides grounded in the actual seams (e.g. where a new tool is registered, where a vendor is bound).

pages.title: Frontend app shell and connectivity

instructions: Explain the module-global connection manager (RpcPromise swap on break, wake probes) and why useState holds wrapped objects.

pages.title: Gadget iframe sandbox and gatekeeper UI hosting
pages.purpose: Client-side sandboxing: the sandboxed iframe with CSP, Cap'n Web injection via data URLs, postMessage handshake, console/escape forwarding; and how gatekeeper configurator/app UIs are hosted similarly.
instructions: Cover error reporting isolation for gatekeeper frames (postMessage, origin null).
Explain the doubly-nested data URL trick, the sandbox attribute, and what the parent frame offers (gadget DO stub via MessagePort).

pages.title: Workspace UI: editor, chat, and actions
pages.purpose: The workspace page: GadgetEditor and CodeMirror OT editing, chat interface streaming, proposed-changes review and merge/revert, the action log and approval UI, auto-approval settings, connections panel, and share modal.
instructions: Ground the OT sync (submitCodeChange/subscribeToCode) and the actions subscription flow in the code.

pages.title: Gatekeeper architecture and lifecycle
pages.purpose: The vendor/user/instance tier model, how gatekeepers install as overseer facets, binding-name management, the UI frames (configurator + full app), the agent catalog, ambient capsules, and external message gateways.
instructions: Cover GatekeeperUiFrame hosting (sandboxed iframe + MessagePort RPC) and the admin-config enabled/disabled gates.
Cover getGatekeeperClassFor chain (vendor -> user DO -> class), facet installation, and the suggestedBindingName flow.

pages.title: Cloudflare gatekeeper: sign-in, billing, and telemetry
pages.purpose: The Cloudflare gatekeeper's three purposes: auth (verified email), AI Gateway billing resources, and Workers Observability read-only telemetry; plus its triple-defence model against provider quirks.
instructions: Cover the resource granularity mapping (account vs worker) to the single scope, and why [] differs from omitted resourceUrlPatterns.
Summarize the three provider behaviours that are never trusted, from the package README/source.

pages.title: Context Library gatekeeper
pages.purpose: The auto-provisioned Context Library: singleton account, three Durable Objects, sharing domains, public/private collections, agent read session and catalog, slash commands, and management UI.
instructions: Cover how the singleton is auto-provided as an ambient capsule and read as observations.
Explain the sharingDomain namespacing and why binding props carry it.

pages.title: MCP connectors: gatekeeper-mcp and gatekeeper-mcp-portal
pages.purpose: The two MCP-speaking gatekeepers and mcp-shared: the tools.ts trust boundary, byo/vetted tiers, scope grammar, at-most-once action store, OAuth chain, bounded limits, and SSRF-safe fetch.
instructions: Explain the owner-only sharing rule for MCP bindings.
Ground the trust tiers and at-most-once semantics in the code; quote the limits table only as documented in mcp-shared/README.md.

pages.title: OAuth connectors: GitHub, Google, and friends
pages.purpose: The common OAuth connect lifecycle shared by the OAuth gatekeepers: connectAccount with nonce, connect callback DO, credentialsExpired/restored, reconnect, incremental scopes for sign-in, and the per-vendor resource model including BigQuery/Sheets/Docs.
instructions: Document the shared shape (nonce-protected connect URL, callback Fetcher, token storage in account DO) and where packages vary.
State which claims are per-vendor specifics vs common contract; mark anything not verified in code as uncertain.

pages.title: Scheduled Tasks gatekeeper
pages.purpose: The scheduler: auto-provisioned singleton, ScheduleDriver Durable Object, alarm-driven delivery, run admission and recovery, caps, and the read-only management UI.
instructions: Ground the alarm/delivery flow, caps (500/account, 100/workspace), and hook enablement split between the driver and the Workshop Connections UI.

pages.title: Agent context compaction
pages.purpose: How long chats stay within the model window: compaction triggers, checkpoints, the summarization call, chatChangeStatuses/foldProposedChanges, and replay-from-checkpoint semantics.
instructions: Ground the trigger ratios, token limits, checkpoint storage shape, and /compact slash command behavior in the code.

pages.title: The AI agent: tools, code mode, and chat flow
pages.purpose: The coding agent: runAgent loop over pi-ai, the tool set (executeCode, file tools, createGadget, setGadgetBinding, listBlueprints, webFetch, connections), chat message model, bindings/env, agent callbacks and spawners, chat attachments, and slash commands.

Cover usage checks before turns and how agent outputs stream to clients.

pages.title: Blueprints: sharing gadget code as templates

pages.title: Code storage: git object store and operational-transform changes
pages.purpose: Where gadget code lives: the refless git object store in each Overseer DO, Yjs as uncommitted chat representation, the CodeChange OT wire format with validation/transform/compose, three-way merges, and the git migration.
instructions: Cover ChatCodeBase, commit pinning, merge-into-chat semantics from plans/git-storage.md.
Explain the two-stage validation order (schema before transform, content after) and the priority convention as fixed invariants.

pages.title: Gadget execution: facets, sandboxing, and exports
pages.purpose: How gadget code runs: WorkerLoader dynamic workers, facet lifecycle and abort/restart semantics, the code-mode harness (disallow_importable_env, null outbound), gadget DO + [restore] persistent stubs, and browser/PDF export.

pages.title: Backend server entrypoints, sessions, and auth

Explain the three auth modes and how AUTH_GATEKEEPERS/DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH are env-driven and deliberately outside AdminConfig.

pages.title: UserDurableObject: identity, accounts, and registries
